A recording can't be checked by code, so these are the caller's claims. Code compares any account read out with the one on file, and never lets a voice confirm a payment or a bank change.

Risk specialist · verdict likely_fraud

A voicemail claiming to be from a supplier's accounts department asks Ashgrove Bakery to update payment details to new bank accounts, with same-day urgency because the old account closes Friday. This is a classic bank-detail-change fraud pattern delivered via an unusual channel.

Skeptic · argues benign

The message arrived through Ashgrove's own voicemail system, with no attachment or link to click and no request for passwords or gift cards. The caller ID 01632 960777 matches the callback number given in the message, and the caller names himself, Rob Kale, and his company, KestrelByte Posting, while providing the full sort code and account number for the bakery to check. That is consistent with a vendor proactively notifying a customer of a banking move, rather than relying on the urgency alone.

What would change my mind: Call KestrelByte Posting on a telephone number already on file and not the 01632 960777 number in the voicemail, and ask whether it changed banks and authorised Rob Kale to request this payment-detail update.
